title: Overview
content:
Example Inventory System is a demo asset that ships with this website template. It exists to show how a complete product page looks, including working documentation with copyable code examples.

The code samples below use an imaginary `ExampleInventory` component. When you write your own documentation, replace them with your asset's real API and usage examples.

title: Requirements
content:
This section is where you'd list everything users need before installing your asset, for example the minimum Unity version, supported render pipelines, or other packages yours depends on.

The demo asset itself has no requirements: it's placeholder content, so there's nothing to install.

title: Installation
content:
Describe how to install your asset here. Most Unity assets are installed in one of two ways:

- Import the package from your Unity Asset Store library (Window > Package Manager > My Assets).
- Or download the package from itch.io and import the .unitypackage via Assets > Import Package.

If your asset needs extra steps, such as scene setup, layers or define symbols, a separate Setup section like the one below is a good place for them.

title: Setup
content:
Explain the first steps after installation. For this demo, imagine the system needs a single component on a GameObject:

- Create an empty GameObject, for example `InventoryHolder`.
- Add the `ExampleInventory` component to it.
- Set the number of slots in the Inspector.
- Call `Initialize` from your own code before using the inventory.

title: Basic Usage
Working With Items
content:
The inventory exposes a small API for the most common item operations. All modifying methods return a `bool`, so you can react when an operation fails, for example when the inventory is full.

- `AddItem(itemId, amount)` adds items and returns false if there is no room.
- `RemoveItem(itemId, amount)` removes items and returns false if there aren't enough.
- `CountItem(itemId)` returns how many items of that type are stored.
- `Clear()` empties the whole inventory.

Note
content: Remember to unsubscribe from static events in `OnDisable`, as shown above. Otherwise you risk keeping references to destroyed objects alive.

title: Troubleshooting
content:
A short list of common problems and their fixes works well here:

- **Nothing happens when I call AddItem:** make sure you called `Initialize` first.
- **Events fire twice:** the event was probably subscribed twice. Subscribe in `OnEnable` and unsubscribe in `OnDisable`.
- **Items disappear between scenes:** the inventory does not persist by default, so save its contents yourself.
